answers: You can temporarily take Donald Trump out of real estate, but you can't take the real estate out of Donald Trump. That much was clear at a Singapore press conference Tuesday, which took place after the president's meeting with Kim Jong Un and in which he touched upon the potential of North Korea's coastline. "They have great beaches," Trump noted, per the Washington Examiner. "You see that whenever they're exploding their cannons into the ocean." And that spectacular view got him to thinking: "Wouldn't that make a great condo? Instead of doing that you could have the best hotels in the world right there. Think of it from a real estate perspective, you have South Korea, you have China, and they own the land in the middle, how bad is that, right? It's great." The AP also reports on another post-summit activity, which it deems a "classic alpha male move": Trump showing off "The Beast," the presidential limousine, to the North Korean leader. CNN shows a video clip of the two men approaching the limo, a Secret Service agent opening the door, and Kim peering in to take a look. "We know that these men were trying to find ways to bond, in just like a personal, human way, and what's more natural for guys [than] to want to check out one another's car," Chris Cuomo notes. (Here are seven complimentary things Trump said about Kim after the summit.)

On Tuesday, President Donald Trump made headlines with a series of remarks and actions during a press conference following his historic summit with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in Singapore. Trump highlighted the potential of North Korea's untapped property market, suggesting that the country could benefit from opening up its economy by developing luxury real estate along its coastline. He humorously remarked that the country's beaches, which are often visible during military exercises, could be transformed into "the best hotel in the world." Trump also shared a video simulation with Kim, showcasing potential development projects in North Korea, which he believed the leader found interesting.

In addition to economic incentives, Trump claimed that North Korea had agreed to relinquish its nuclear weapons and was ready to work toward a lasting peace and complete denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula. He expressed optimism about the progress made during the summit, despite the challenges of negotiating with a nation known for its isolationism.

During the summit, Trump also took the opportunity to showcase his presidential limousine, "The Beast," to Kim Jong Un. The moment, which initially caused some confusion, was interpreted as a display of Trump's confidence and a classic "alpha male" gesture. Trump had previously stated that he would be able to determine the success of the summit within minutes of meeting with Kim.

This initiative, known as "No More 404," aims to maintain the integrity of online content and provide users with access to historical web pages even as they are updated or removed.

In summary, the news highlights a mix of political developments, technological initiatives, and symbolic gestures that reflect the complex and multifaceted nature of global affairs. From Trump's bold statements on North Korea's economic potential to the Internet Archive's mission to preserve the web, these events underscore the ongoing efforts to shape the future of international relations and digital information.
